I transferred an S&S ISA from Vanguard which took around 7-8 weeks. After I chased, it did finally land in my account the next day. By the time it arrived, I invested in the stocks that I had been tracking for weeks but unfortunately it was too late - invested at ATHs and the market dived soon after and I’m still paying for it now. But transfers can take time and I decided not to put this down to T212 solely.

Next I tried to partially transfer a workplace pension (while keeping it open to continue contributions). I accept these are more complex but again it was extremely slow to the point where they said they had not heard a response from my workplace provider. I called up my workplace provider to enquire why and they said T212 had not responded on the Origo transfer system to their question about whether it was a 95% or 100% transfer (for reference, I had ordered a 95.2% transfer). I went back to T212 and told them how to action the request - I did not receive an apology but was at least satisfied they actioned it. I understand it’s my money and my responsibility but why does the customer constantly have to follow-up if T212 fails to respond to a message? My workplace provider gave me a transfer date on the phone and I will maintain contact with T212 through the app as that seems to be the only way to contact them. 

Overall, the app experience has been great and I don’t have any burning issues with it, but transfers have been something I would advise people to be proactive and vigilant about. It’s been a mixed first few months but look forward to continue to use the app once the transfers have been sorted out.

I first started using 212 this year January and I must say it’s not half bad when it comes to their stocks and shares accounts. As a new investor I’ve made my fair share of money especially in a year like 2026. But my problem with 212 is this, the cfds are absolutely choppy and laggy and a scam account to rob you. For those who don’t know, cfds are otc (over the counter) leveraged derivatives and your broker takes the other side of the trade. Naturally you profiting means they need to pay you even if their entire clientele takes the same side of the trade and it turns out to be a winner. Now this very morning as the market opened it was very clear that a certain asset was going to go up in value after certain news came out. At the open of the London session it absolutely froze. A message came up displaying “You can place market orders after the instrument receives a new price. Pending orders are still accepted”. Not even allowing me to close my overnight positions that were in the opposite direction. Not only did I miss out on the opportunity to make a couple quid, I lost more than I would have if only i had been allowed to close my trade. Further more i see real time price differences for identical assets in the stocks and shares account and the cfd account. This broker doesn’t want you to win. They’re as good as wall street in the US. They want your liquidity they want you bankrupt. And they don’t want to pay you a dime even when you’re in the right. Thanks for ruining my morning. I’ll be changing brokers soon.

This app's flat, disorganized presentation makes it incredibly difficult to get a quick, holistic view of my positions, forcing me to mentally piece together information that the app should be organizing for me. For complex strategies, this makes the app borderline unusable and dangerous.
